# s166 — Hint at show instead of printing the slice path

Plain `next` prints the slice JSON path under the id. That path is why an agent opens the tracking file instead of calling show.

**Findings:** another project opened a slice JSON file because next printed its path · **Size:** S · **Tree:** cli

**Not in this slice:** removing `path` from JSON; changing `list`, `show`, or `status`; hiding the path when `--json` is set.

## Why

`_next_fields` and `_ready_entry` append the slice path whenever the file exists. `next`, `next --ready`, `next --show`, and `next --batch` all use those helpers, so every text result ends with a path such as `.slicer/slices/S15.json`. `--json --lean` already drops `path` on an item object. The text line is the footgun.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`_next_fields`, `_ready_entry`, the `next` options)
- `docs/commands.md` and `docs/agents.md` (the `next` text shape)
- `tests/test_cli.py` and any next-batch text test that asserts the path line
- `CHANGELOG.md`

## Failing tests

1. Text for `next`, `next --ready`, `next --show`, and a batch prints `slicer show ID` when the item has a slice, and does not print the slice path.
2. An item with no slice keeps the existing promote hint and does not gain a show hint.
3. A text-only flag, `--path`, adds the path line back. JSON still includes `path`. `--lean` still drops it on an item object.
4. `list`, `show`, and `status` text are unchanged.

## Implement

Stop appending the path in the text helpers. When the item has a slice, print a show hint that names the id. Keep the promote hint when it does not. Add `--path` to print the path line as well. Leave the JSON object, including `path`, as it is.

## Check

The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.
